Answer: C
Reason: The chest X-ray shows a widened left superior mediastinum (indicated by the arrow) and slight left ventricular enlargement, which are classic radiographic signs of a Persistent Left Superior Vena Cava (PLSVC). When a PLSVC drains directly into the left atrium (unroofed coronary sinus), it creates a right-to-left shunt, explaining the patient's mild hypoxaemia and dyspnoea without pulmonary congestion.
